newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia pulp labor talks to start soon.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia pulp labor talks to start soon.

text.p: The two unions representing pulp and paper workers in British Columbia expect to begin negotiations with Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd later this month, a union official said Monday.

The unions have targeted Fletcher to set a pattern contract for the industry. The Communications, Energy and Paperworkers union and Pulp, Paper and Wookworkers on Canada union expect that a labor agreement with Fletcher will then be copied by other companies in the British Columbia industry.
CEP official Brian Payne said Monday the unions would probably meet to exchange proposals with the company during the third week of March.
About 2,400 workers at Fletcher are covered by that agreement. In total, the sector includes about 14,000 workers in British Columbia.
Payne said Fletcher wants to bargain separately at each location, but the unions remain hopeful that the talks will be consolidated into a single set of negotiations.
